description: Camp bronze on a ribbed wooden grip, made for rope and rations. It comes off a mule that is carrying nothing.
lore: It is sold as a trophy and it is a bread knife. Soft bronze, the edge honed back three fingers' worth over years, a guard on it because guards were the fashion where it was made and not because anything was ever coming the other way. [[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] has had a dozen of them across her bench and says the same thing about every one: this has never been fought with. It cut rope. It cut rations. It went back in the roll clean.

Buyers hear that and pay the thirty-two gold anyway, because a knife that came down off [[monsters/dark_donkey|an animal still walking the old east road]] is a story and a bread knife is not. Sigrun does not argue them out of it. Her view is that they have the better story and have picked the wrong reason for wanting it — somebody packed this for a journey, with cheese and a length of rope, and the journey is still going.
gm_notes: Sigrun as a reader of edges rather than a widow — use her professionally as often as possible so the one time she is not lands. Trophy pricing is sentiment; she prices the hand that held it.
